title: Hash-chained Audit Ledger
intent: Make ordered audit history tamper-evident with predecessor-bound hashes.
problem: Without each entry hashes canonical content plus predecessor hash, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the hash-chained audit ledger contract.
context: This pattern addresses audit ordering must reveal tampering; its concrete control is each entry hashes canonical content plus predecessor hash.
forces: Correctness requires that entry order is cryptographically committed
Operational pressure can cause: history rows are edited without recomputing descendants
solution: Implement each entry hashes canonical content plus predecessor hash. Verify the anchored symbol `OrchestratorStorageError` with `test_task_contract_canonical_round_trip` before reuse.
invariants: chain verification starts from a defined genesis
failure_modes: history rows are edited without recomputing descendants
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `history rows are edited without recomputing descendants` and fails closed if the hash-chained audit ledger evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For hash-chained audit ledger, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to each entry hashes canonical content plus predecessor hash.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: audit ordering must reveal tampering
Do not apply when: cryptographic non-repudiation requires an external signature service
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
not_when: cryptographic non-repudiation requires an external signature service
